analysis:
Both units are head-side text of docs/provider/cli-reference.md (lines 1213-2130) and I found no security regression in them. The changes visible here are documentation only: the `sandbox setup` plan and slot-change flow, the `--disk` work-disk option, the installer `--plan --json-progress` contract, and the `Work disk` report lines. The rest of the file is unchanged surrounding text. The patch excerpt is truncated, so the `--disk` path-validation text around the Setup section (head lines ~1094-1132) was not visible.

Controls the docs state, relevant to TB-013, T-061 and A-019:
- Setup never passes the installer's `--force`.
- Without a terminal or with `--yes`, setup applies a plan only when it adds slots and removes none.
- Otherwise it prints `Not applied` and the command that applies the plan.
- Plan JSON is parsed leniently and ignores unknown members.
- A plan with a wrong schema or missing numbers is rejected.
- `status --json` is decoded leniently and bounded by timeouts.
- A failed plan under `--disk` stops setup rather than falling back.

Open questions for later review of the actual Swift code (SandboxSetupProgress.swift, SandboxAddon.swift and the `--disk` handling). Those files are not in this batch.
- Whether path canonicalization and symlink/`/Volumes` checks for `--disk` are implemented as documented.
- Whether adding external work disks widens TB-013 and A-019, since add-on VM images and jobs would sit on removable media. This is a possible threat-model update, not a demonstrated regression.
- Whether the unattended `--yes` auto-apply of slot increases is bounded by the installer.

The cache and TB-007 text (T-041) is only mentioned in passing in the status docs. The `prefix_cache=` status vocabulary is unchanged and discloses no new sensitive data.
